intent: Make every terminal projection and persisted preview render runtime_activity.v1 as current lease evidence, observed nonterminal records, and expired-or-unproven records without implying executor liveness, while preserving explicitly legacy status-count payloads.

negative_controls.name: lease-semantics-downgrade-must-fail
negative_controls.command: python3 -c "import pathlib, subprocess, sys; p=pathlib.Path('terminal/src/protocol.ts'); t=p.read_text(); a='  return activitySemantics === RUNTIME_ACTIVITY_SEMANTICS;'; a in t or sys.exit(3); p.write_text(t.replace(a, '  return false;', 1)); sys.exit(subprocess.run(['bun', 'test', 'terminal/tests/protocol.test.ts', '--test-name-pattern', 'runtime_activity.v1']).returncode)"

commit.message: fix: label runtime lease evidence truthfully

interface_mismatches: Legacy terminal payloads use active_* names for raw status counts, while runtime_activity.v1 keeps those fields only as compatibility aliases for current identity-bound leases.
CanonicalRuntimeSnapshot.active_session_count and active_run_count become current-lease counts under runtime_activity.v1; total sessions and runs remain in metadata.overview.
Text fallback output now carries two self-describing metric lines; reading only the first silently discards observed-nonterminal, expired-or-unproven, and liveness qualifications.

Persisted summaries, compact app rows, repo/control parsers, and component-level inventory parsers can reintroduce false active labels after the protocol boundary unless the semantic marker is preserved and consumed end to end.
A current lease is bounded persistence evidence and explicitly does not prove a live executor process.
honest_blockers: Legacy payloads without activity_semantics must retain their historical active-status labels because the terminal cannot reinterpret their producer semantics safely.
Any present but unknown activity_semantics must fail closed and must not inherit legacy active labels.
The UI can present current lease evidence and executor-liveness uncertainty but cannot probe or prove operating-system process liveness.
Persisted previews created before runtime_activity.v1 may still contain legacy prose; a fresh typed snapshot rebuilds and replaces those activity labels at the protocol boundary.
The exact work-packet positive-command allowlist does not admit Bun; targeted terminal tests and TypeScript checking run directly and in CI rather than through the packet evaluator.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the UI truth-label commit. The Python runtime activity classifier remains authoritative, but terminal projections and persisted previews will again display compatibility aliases as active status labels.
